metadata.title: The Dehn Canon: Lean 4 formalization (PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000003)
metadata.description:
Lean 4 formalization accompanying DICTO's paper #113, The Dehn Canon (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24383552). It proves: Dehn's answer to Hilbert's third problem, with the Dehn invariant defined from the solid as a set of points: Hilbert's two tetrahedra on one base are neither scissors congruent nor equicomplementable; the set-defined invariant equals the classical edge sum of length ⊗ dihedral angle; scissors-congruent convex polytopes have the same invariant; and no similar copy of the regular tetrahedron is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the cube.

Built with Lean 4 (leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2) with Mathlib at commit 0653561 (tag v4.35.0-rc2). This archive is the GitHub repository DICTOR-Master/dehn-canon-lean at commit 9ea20f6dfd64fc3f10f64b1fb59a754a77e5cf57, registered in the Palomar registry as PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000003-v1 at this commit; every proof is checked by the Lean kernel.
